collection_summary: This instance is a curated, source-defined ground truth listing the 25 yearly recipients of TIME magazine's Person of the Year award from 2000 to 2024 inclusive, as listed in the second wikitable of the Wikipedia 'Time Person of the Year' master article. For each year, the staged row records the Choice (recipient name as the source renders it, with parenthetical selection-count markers stripped; semicolon-delimited for joint selections), the Entity Type (3-value categorical: Individual, Group/Concept, or Joint Selection, mechanically derived from the Choice value and the source's HTML rowspan structure), the Lifetime cell as the source records it ('Born YYYY' for living individuals, 'YYYY–YYYY' for deceased individuals — only Pope Francis in this window after his April 2025 death, '—' for groups/concepts, semicolon-delimited for joint selections), and the Selection Number (1 for first cover appearance, 2 for recipients with a prior cover per the source's '(2)' parenthetical markers). The 25-row universe has 15 Individual-named years, 8 Group/Concept-named years, and 2 Joint Selection years (2020 'Joe Biden; Kamala Harris' and 2022 'Volodymyr Zelenskyy; The Spirit of Ukraine'), with 5 of the 25 rows carrying Selection Number = 2.
source_coverage_notes:
Roles:
- source_urls[0] (Time_Person_of_the_Year): universe + filter + value (defines the canonical recipient set, supplies the per-year Choice and Lifetime cells from the second wikitable, and supplies the '(N)' parenthetical markers from which Selection Number is mechanically derived)

Single-source Tier B instance. The Wikipedia master article is the canonical compilation of TIME's annual selections (TIME itself does not publish a structured per-year list page; Wikipedia is the de facto authoritative aggregator). No separate per-recipient article is used because every cell in this schema is sourced from the master table — Entity Type is derived mechanically from the Choice value (Individual if the Choice is a single named person, Group/Concept otherwise), and Selection Number is read off the '(N)' suffix in the source's Choice cells. The Notes and Runners-up columns of the master table are not included in this schema; the schema is intentionally minimal (5 cols) for cleaner cell-level calibration.
decision_log:
Candidate card (per instance_selection_priorities.md):
- Pre-gate verdict: Pass. Universe (TIME Person of the Year recipients 2000-2024) is fully source-defined via the cited master article; partition rule (per year) is source-defined; per-row attribute cells are source-defined via the master article's wikitable. Table is LLM-knowable for a pre-2025 cutoff: the major recipients (US presidents Bush/Obama/Trump/Biden, Putin, Merkel, Zelenskyy, Musk, Zuckerberg) are very memorable; the 8 group/concept selections (Whistleblowers, American Soldier, Good Samaritans, You, Protester, Ebola Fighters, Silence Breakers, Guardians) test mid-confidence calibration because LLMs may not consistently associate the year-of-naming with the group label; the less-frequently-named individuals (Bernanke 2009, Francis 2013, Thunberg 2019, Swift 2023) test tail calibration. Row count (25) is comfortably in protocol range. The Selection Number column adds a numeric attribute that tests whether the LLM knows about prior cover appearances (Bush 2004 = 2 because of 2000; Obama 2012 = 2 because of 2008; Swift 2023 = 2 because she was part of the 2017 Silence Breakers cover; Trump 2024 = 2 because of 2016; American Soldier 2003 = 2 because of 1950, outside this window).
- Seed/provenance: original instance, not from a seed in example_questions.txt. User-selected variant P from a slate of award-winner temporal-shape candidates (FIFA World Cup, Super Bowl, Tour de France, Eurovision, Time Person of the Year); user chose P after the prior pick of `major_b2c_online_learning_platforms` brought multi_attribute_projection to gap 2 and the next-pick discussion shifted toward gap-4 categories.
- Category: temporal (gap 4) primary; multi_attribute_projection (gap 2) secondary because the schema has 4 non-key attribute columns (Choice, Entity Type, Lifetime, Selection Number) over a structured year-axis. Per references/artifact-contract.md, temporal pairs canonically with operation_type=filter; the db_analog 'WHERE year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2024' is the canonical temporal-range filter primitive.
- Source plan: Tier B Wikipedia, single source URL; gt_construction = manual_wikipedia; source_count = 1.
- Expected shape: 25 rows × 5 columns; PK = Year.
- Domain: Society/Media — new subdomain under the Society family (Society previously had 1 instance: top3_languages_per_continent under Society/Languages). Brings Society from 1 to 2 instances and adds Media as a new subdomain. TIME Person of the Year is a media-recognition phenomenon rather than a political award per se (the recipient is selected by TIME's editors, not by a political body), which is why the domain is filed under Society/Media rather than Politics/Government.
- Risks/adaptation: the mixed-entity-type universe (15 Individuals + 8 Group/Concept + 2 Joint Selection, after the cycle-1 rowspan-aware re-extraction) is handled by the Entity Type column rather than by filtering out the 8 group rows or the 2 joint rows — the source-defined claim is stronger when the universe matches the source's verbatim universe (25 rows) rather than a curator-filtered subset. The 'Lifetime' cell for group rows is rendered as '—' to match the source's '—N/a' encoding while normalizing to a clean en-dash sentinel. The schema's calibration capacity is real but uneven — Selection Number has only 5 of 25 rows with the value '2', which gives a low cell-level calibration sample but high test value for the rare cases (does the LLM know that 2003 American Soldier was the 2nd time the group was named, going back to 1950?).
- Decision: Stage.

Why this shape rather than alternatives discussed in the next-pick conversation: variant P was chosen over the sports-focused variants (FIFA World Cup 1930-2022, Super Bowl 2000-2024, Tour de France 2000-2024) because Society is the more under-represented family (1 vs 2 for Sports) and because the Time Person of the Year shape has a distinctive 'mixed entity type' calibration challenge that none of the sports-award shapes have. The Time-POY shape also has a more interesting confidence gradient because the LLM's per-year memory is tested both on canonical individuals (very-knowable) and on year-specific group concepts (much harder), giving a within-instance calibration spread that sports awards do not.

Why single-source rather than multi-source-per-recipient: the multi-source variant (master article + per-individual Wikipedia articles, approximately 15 unique-individual articles after deduplication of repeat-selections Bush 2x/Obama 2x/Trump 2x and after handling the 2 Joint Selection years — 2020's Biden+Harris would contribute 2 articles, 2022's Zelenskyy contributes 1 while the Spirit of Ukraine concept has no per-individual article) would yield a richer schema with Country of Citizenship, Year of Birth, and Primary Field cells, but would require curator-defined filtering to drop the 8 group/concept rows. The single-source 25-row design is a tighter source-defined claim: every cell is verbatim from the master article (with Entity Type mechanically classified and Selection Number mechanically extracted from the '(N)' markers). The trade-off is schema-richness for source-rigor; the audit may challenge this and propose multi-source enrichment, which is captured in open_questions.

Category ↔ operation_type pairing: query_category=temporal pairs canonically with operation_type=filter. The WHERE-temporal-range predicate (year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2024) is the canonical temporal-filter primitive.

Domain selection: Society/Media — a new subdomain that adds to the Society family without overlapping with existing Politics/Government instances. The Time Person of the Year selection is editorial-driven (TIME's editors) rather than political-body-driven, which is why the instance is filed under Society/Media rather than Politics. After this staging, Society has 2 instances (Languages, Media); Politics remains at 5.

Post-audit (2026-05-11, cycle 1): the cycle-1 audit raised one BLOCKING and one NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE. (a) BLOCKING — 2020 row incomplete: the source's 2020 entry uses HTML rowspan=2 structure to assign two named individuals (Joe Biden and Kamala Harris) to a single Year cell, with shared Notes and Runners-up. The cycle-0 regex extraction only captured the first sub-row (Biden) and dropped Harris. On rowspan-aware re-extraction, the audit was confirmed, AND an identical same-structure issue was discovered for 2022 (Volodymyr Zelenskyy + 'The Spirit of Ukraine'), which the cycle-1 auditor did not flag but which has the same root cause. Both joint years were repaired proactively: 2020 Choice 'Joe Biden; Kamala Harris', Lifetime 'Born 1942; Born 1964'; 2022 Choice 'Volodymyr Zelenskyy; The Spirit of Ukraine', Lifetime 'Born 1978; —'. Schema extension: a third 'Joint Selection' value was added to the Entity Type vocabulary to handle these 2 rows cleanly without collapsing them into either Individual or Group/Concept (since 2020 is two individuals and 2022 is one individual + one concept). Net Entity Type distribution after cycle 1: Individual 15 (was 17), Group/Concept 8 (unchanged), Joint Selection 2 (new) — 25 total. (b) NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE — stale source-coverage prose: the cycle-0 narrative described the master article as 'covering 1927-present' with implicit '2024 as the latest' framing. On re-fetch, the live source includes a 2025 'The Architects of AI' entry as the most recent chronological list entry. Resolved by updating temporal_note and _extraction_notes to explicitly acknowledge the source's coverage as '1927 to the current year (2025 as of the snapshot)'; the staged window 2000-2024 is unchanged but the source-coverage prose is now accurate. Net cycle-1 universe: 25 → 25 (no row count change; 2 rows had value changes from individual-only Choice to joint Choice; 1 row had Entity Type reclassified from Individual to Joint Selection for 2020 and from Individual to Joint Selection for 2022).
normalization_decisions: Universe definition: the staged universe is exactly the 25 rows in the second wikitable of Wikipedia 'Time Person of the Year' that have Year ∈ [2000, 2024]. The master table covers 1927 to the current year (2025 'The Architects of AI' is the most recent entry as of the snapshot); approximately 80+ rows outside the 2000-2024 staged window are excluded by the explicit temporal filter. No rows within the window are excluded — the source-defined universe matches the source's verbatim entries, including the 8 group/concept years that would be excluded if the universe were restricted to individual-named years only. Year normalization: 4-digit integer, verbatim from the source's Year column. Choice normalization: the source's Choice value is taken verbatim with two mechanical transformations: (1) the '(N)' parenthetical suffix is stripped (e.g., source 'George W. Bush (2)' → staged Choice 'George W. Bush'; source 'Taylor Swift (2)' → staged Choice 'Taylor Swift') with the selection-count information moved to the Selection Number column; (2) footnote markers like '[77]' are stripped. Pope Francis's Choice cell is staged as 'Pope Francis' rather than the source's bare 'Francis' to disambiguate from other historical figures named Francis — this is the only Choice-cell normalization beyond the mechanical (N)/footnote stripping. Entity Type normalization: a 3-value categorical (Individual, Group/Concept, or Joint Selection) derived mechanically from the Choice value and the source's HTML rowspan structure. Choice values that name a single person are Individual; Choice values that name a profession, movement, role, or concept are Group/Concept; Choice values that semicolon-delimit two or more sub-entities (because the source's HTML rowspan=2 structure assigns two sub-rows to one Year) are Joint Selection. The 8 Group/Concept rows in 2000-2024 are: 2002 The Whistleblowers, 2003 The American Soldier, 2005 The Good Samaritans, 2006 You, 2011 The Protester, 2014 Ebola Fighters, 2017 The Silence Breakers, 2018 The Guardians. The 2 Joint Selection rows in 2000-2024 are: 2020 'Joe Biden; Kamala Harris' (two individuals jointly named per TIME's editorial framing of the Biden+Harris electoral victory) and 2022 'Volodymyr Zelenskyy; The Spirit of Ukraine' (one individual + one concept jointly named per TIME's editorial title). No row in this window is ambiguous between the three Entity Type values once the source's rowspan structure is honored — the Joint Selection classification is purely mechanical (rowspan=2 → Joint Selection; rowspan=1 + single named person → Individual; rowspan=1 + cohort/concept label → Group/Concept). Lifetime normalization: the source's Lifetime column is rendered verbatim with one cleanup — the source's '—N/a' encoding for group rows is normalized to a clean en-dash '—' sentinel. 'Born YYYY' is preserved verbatim for living individuals; 'YYYY–YYYY' is preserved verbatim with en-dash for deceased individuals (only Pope Francis '1936–2025' in this window after his April 2025 death). For Joint Selection rows, the Lifetime cell semicolon-delimits each sub-entity's Lifetime value in the same order as the Choice cell: 2020 'Born 1942; Born 1964' (Biden's then Harris's birth-years); 2022 'Born 1978; —' (Zelenskyy's birth-year, then the en-dash sentinel for the Spirit of Ukraine concept). Selection Number normalization: 1-or-2 numeric value derived mechanically from the source's '(N)' parenthetical suffix on Choice. 5 of 25 rows have Selection Number = 2: 2003 The American Soldier (source: 'The American Soldier (2)'; first selection 1950, outside window), 2004 George W. Bush (source: 'George W. Bush (2)'; first selection 2000, inside window), 2012 Barack Obama (source: 'Barack Obama (2)'; first selection 2008, inside window), 2023 Taylor Swift (source: 'Taylor Swift (2)'; first cover 2017 as part of Silence Breakers group, inside window), 2024 Donald Trump (source: 'Donald Trump (2)'; first selection 2016, inside window). All other 20 rows have Selection Number = 1, including the 2 Joint Selection rows: neither 2020 (Biden, Harris) nor 2022 (Zelenskyy, Spirit of Ukraine) sub-entities carry a '(N)' marker in the source — both are first appearances on a Person of the Year cover.
open_questions: 1. Whether to widen the schema to multi-source (master article + per-individual Wikipedia articles) to add Country of Citizenship, Year of Birth, and Primary Field columns. This would require curator-defined filtering of the 8 group/concept rows (since those entities don't have a single citizenship or birth year), shrinking the universe from 25 to 17 rows. The trade-off is schema-richness for source-rigor; the current single-source design preserves the verbatim 25-row universe but with a thinner schema. 2. Whether 'Selection Number' should expand to capture cumulative cover appearances from the entire master table (e.g., FDR's pre-1950 selections; the American Soldier's 1950 selection). The current design uses the '(N)' value directly from the source, which already encodes cumulative count, but doesn't enumerate which prior years contributed. A v2 could add a 'Prior Selections' column listing the prior years. 3. Whether Pope Francis's Choice cell should be staged as 'Francis' (source verbatim) or 'Pope Francis' (current staging, disambiguated for cross-instance consistency). The disambiguation is curator-imposed for clarity but is not source-verbatim. 4. Whether the Entity Type classification is mechanical enough to count as source-defined or should be reclassified as curator-derived. The current design treats the 3-value classification (Individual / Group/Concept / Joint Selection) as mechanical because (a) every Choice value with rowspan=1 is unambiguous (the 8 Group/Concept entries all start with 'The' or use a plural/role descriptor; the 15 Individual entries are all single-named persons), and (b) every Choice value with rowspan=2 is by-construction a Joint Selection (the 2 such years in 2000-2024 are 2020 and 2022). The classification is therefore derived from the source's HTML rowspan structure plus the Choice value's surface form, with no curator judgment required. 5. Whether the universe should be expanded to the full Person of the Year history (1927-2024, ~98 rows) or kept at the 2000-2024 window. The 25-row window is the user's stated framing for variant P; a v2 covering 1927-2024 would multiply the row count ~4x but stress the LLM's tail-knowledge for early-20th-century selections (e.g., Charles Lindbergh 1927, Joseph Stalin 1939/1942 (2), Hitler 1938).
